cards.name: Born in 1962
cards.known_for: Turns a temporary site into a permanent institution
cards.lore: Temporary site for Surulere, permanent vibes for Akoka. Na so legends start.
cards.fact: UNILAG was established by University of Lagos Act No. 11 of 1962. Lectures began on 22 October 1962 at a temporary site in Surulere, before the move to Akoka.
cards.question: Who in your family was the first to school in UNILAG?
cards.source_title: UNILAG Historical Odyssey - University Of Lagos

cards.name: Akoka Main Campus
cards.known_for: Lagoon breeze on demand, 802 acres deep
cards.lore: Water views without paying Lekki rent. Akoka understood the assignment.
cards.fact: UNILAG's main campus sits on 802 acres of land at Akoka and is largely surrounded by the Lagos Lagoon.
cards.question: Which shortcut across the Akoka campus did you swear by?

cards.name: In Deed and in Truth
cards.known_for: Wins any school argument in one sentence
cards.lore: Say it with your chest: First Choice, Nation's Pride.
cards.fact: UNILAG's motto is 'In deed and in truth', and its official slogan is 'University of First Choice and the Nation's Pride'.
cards.question: Is UNILAG really the University of First Choice? Defend your answer.

cards.name: J.F. Ade Ajayi Auditorium
cards.known_for: Turns any gathering into a big UNILAG moment
cards.lore: Call am Main Audi or call am Ade Ajayi. Just no come late.
cards.fact: The J.F. Ade Ajayi Auditorium, formerly the Main Auditorium, honours historian Prof. J.F. Ade Ajayi, UNILAG's third Vice-Chancellor (1972 to 1978).
cards.question: What's the most memorable event you attended at the Main Auditorium?
cards.geo_note: place not found, centre of its area
cards.source_title: History of Vice Chancellors - University Of Lagos

cards.name: Hall Roll Call
cards.known_for: Turns strangers into hall family for life
cards.lore: Your hall is your tribe. Choose wisely, defend loudly.
cards.fact: Jaja, Moremi, Kofo Ademola, Fagunwa and Madam Tinubu are among UNILAG's halls of residence. All five reopened to students in June 2025 after renovation works.
cards.question: Which hall did you stay in, and which hall had the best gist?
cards.source_title: Important Notice: Update on Movement into Halls of Residence

cards.name: UNILAG 103.1 FM
cards.known_for: Broadcasts campus gist at the speed of sound
cards.lore: Campus gist with a licence. Tune in, no dull.
cards.fact: UNILAG got its radio licence in 2002, and UNILAG 103.1 FM began broadcasting live in 2004. The station says it was Nigeria's first university radio station to go live.
cards.question: Have you ever been on air at UNILAG 103.1 FM, or called in?
cards.geo_note: place not found, centre of its area

cards.name: Yaba Higher College
cards.known_for: Ships a whole student body to Ibadan and calls it a university
cards.lore: Before Ibadan had a campus, Yaba was already doing the homework.
cards.fact: Founded in Yaba in 1932, it trained Africans in fields like medicine, engineering and teaching. In 1948 its students and equipment moved to Ibadan to start University College, Ibadan.
cards.question: Which school in your family history goes back the furthest?

cards.name: Queen's College
cards.known_for: Produces trailblazing women by the class-load
cards.lore: Pass on the torch, then pass the gist at the reunion.
cards.fact: Opened on 10 October 1927 as the Government School for Girls, Lagos, the first government-owned school for girls. It became Queen's College in 1928 and moved to Yaba in 1958.
cards.question: Who is the most impressive Queen's College old student you know?

cards.name: FSTC Yaba
cards.known_for: Builds engineers before they finish secondary school
cards.lore: Science, tech and Yaba hustle, all on one timetable.
cards.fact: Founded in 1948, Federal Science and Technical College, Yaba is a mixed secondary school and one of over 100 federal government unity schools run by the Federal Ministry of Education.
cards.question: If you could master one technical trade overnight, which would it be?
cards.geo_note: place not found, centre of its area
cards.source_title: Federal Science and Technical College, Yaba - Wikipedia

cards.name: St Finbarr's College
cards.known_for: Turns schoolboys into Super Eagles
cards.lore: Came for the books, left with a first touch.
cards.fact: Founded by Irish priest and football administrator Fr Denis Slattery, St Finbarr's College in Akoka produced Nigerian football stars including the late Stephen Keshi.
cards.question: Which Nigerian footballer would you most want on your five-a-side team?
cards.source_title: Flashback: Longest-stayed football expatriate, Fr Slattery dies - Sports Village Square

cards.name: Tejuosho Market
cards.known_for: Rises from the ashes with extra floors
cards.lore: Come for one item, leave with three bags and zero regrets.
cards.fact: After fire gutted the old Tejuosho market in 2007, a partnership of Lagos State, Stormberg Engineering and First Bank rebuilt it as a large shopping complex on Ojuelegba-Itire Road.
cards.question: What is the best bargain you have ever haggled for at a Lagos market?

cards.name: Yaba Bus Terminal
cards.known_for: Links bus, rail and hustle in one stop
cards.lore: The bus finally has a proper home in Yaba.
cards.fact: Commissioned by the Lagos State Government on 15 June 2021, the LAMATA-built Yaba Bus Terminal was designed to complement the Lagos Rail Mass Transit Red Line.
cards.question: What is your most memorable Lagos bus ride story?
cards.source_title: Lagos Govt Commissions Yaba Bus Terminal - Channels TV

cards.name: Red Line Yaba Station
cards.known_for: Beats the go-slow on steel rails
cards.lore: Agbado to Yaba with no go-slow? Lagos, is this you?
cards.fact: Yaba is one of eight stations on the Lagos Red Line, whose full passenger service started on 15 October 2024 between Agbado and Oyingbo.
cards.question: Where would you go first if a train could take you anywhere in Lagos?
cards.source_title: Red Line Goes Live With Passenger Operation 15th October 2024 - LAMATA

cards.name: CcHub
cards.known_for: Turns a weekend hackathon idea into a real company
cards.lore: Every Yaba tech story has a chapter that starts on Herbert Macaulay Way.
cards.fact: Co-Creation Hub opened in Yaba in 2011 and became the anchor of its tech cluster. In 2019 it acquired Kenya's iHub, which Techpoint called the first time an African tech hub bought another.
cards.question: If you could build one app to fix a Lagos problem, what would it fix?

cards.name: Yabacon Valley
cards.known_for: Gets called five different names and answers to all of them
cards.lore: Silicon Valley who? Yaba has its own valley now.
cards.fact: 'Yabacon Valley', a blend of Yaba and Silicon Valley, is a popular nickname for Yaba's tech cluster. It is still debated, with rivals like Silicon Lagoon, Yaba Right and Yaba iHQ.
cards.question: Yabacon Valley, Silicon Lagoon or just Yaba: what should we call it?
cards.source_title: #Yabacon: How citizens and innovators have transformed Yaba - YAFRI

cards.name: Yaba Left
cards.known_for: Has been caring for Lagos minds for over a century
cards.lore: Mental health is health. Respect to everyone working and healing here.
cards.fact: 'Yaba Left' is Lagos street talk for the Federal Neuro-Psychiatric Hospital, Yaba. It opened in October 1907 as an asylum and is now a federal hospital for mental health care.
cards.question: How can we talk about mental health in Lagos without the jokes?
cards.source_title: From asylum to psychiatric hospital: 113-year journey of 'Yaba Left' - Daily Trust

cards.name: The Adeboruwa Throne
cards.known_for: Summons chiefs, drummers and visitors with one palace call
cards.lore: Igbogbo no be just area o, na full kingdom with royal paperwork.
cards.fact: Igbogbo is a kingdom whose Oba is styled the Adeboruwa of Igbogbo. Its council area, Igbogbo/Bayeku LCDA, is one of the units carved out of the old Ikorodu LGA in 2003.
cards.question: What makes a town feel like a kingdom and not just a neighbourhood?
cards.source_title: Dignitaries celebrate Adeboruwa's 10 years on throne (The Guardian Nigeria)

cards.name: Igbogbo Day
cards.known_for: Pulls Igbogbo sons and daughters home from anywhere
cards.lore: Thirty editions in and Igbogbo still knows how to throw a party with heritage.
cards.fact: Igbogbo Day is the kingdom's yearly cultural celebration. Its 30th edition ended with a packed grand finale at the town stadium, themed 'A festival of new opportunities, land of Cool beauty'.
cards.question: Which hometown celebration would you travel the furthest to attend?
cards.source_title: Igbogbo's rich cultural heritage on display at festival (The Guardian Nigeria)

cards.name: The New Adeboruwa Palace
cards.known_for: Turns any visit into a royal audience
cards.lore: New palace, same royal energy. Greet well when you enter o.
cards.fact: A newly built Adeboruwa of Igbogbo Palace was commissioned for the Lagos State Government, which described the building as a beacon of shared history.
cards.question: What should every palace have that a regular building does not?
cards.geo_note: place not found, centre of its area
cards.source_title: Sanwo-Olu commissions Adeboruwa of Igbogbo Palace (BusinessDay)

cards.name: Adeboruwa Market
cards.known_for: Turns one shopping list into two hundred options
cards.lore: Two hundred shops means two hundred chances to price am well.
cards.fact: Igbogbo has a 200-shop Adeboruwa Market, built through a public-private partnership by the Igbogbo/Baiyeku LCDA.
cards.question: What is the one stall every Lagos market needs?
cards.geo_note: place not found, centre of its area
cards.source_title: As Igbogbo soars under Oba Kasali (Blueprint)

cards.name: Baiyeku Jetty
cards.known_for: Skips road traffic by taking the water way
cards.lore: Traffic who? Baiyeku said make we try the water route.
cards.fact: In June 2020, Lagos handed the newly built Baiyeku Concrete Jetty in Ikorodu over to the Lagos State Waterways Authority (LASWA) to improve water transport in the area.
cards.question: Would you swap your bus commute for a boat ride? Why or why not?
cards.geo_note: moved about 60 m to a viewpoint outside the water zone
cards.source_title: Lagos hands over Baiyeku Jetty to LASWA (BrandSpur)

cards.name: Ikorodu's 1865 Ally
cards.known_for: Shows up for the neighbours when it matters
cards.lore: When Ikorodu called for backup, Igbogbo picked up first.
cards.fact: A 2021 Yoruba Studies Review article credits Balogun Jaiyesimi's diplomacy with forming a coalition of Ikorodu and its neighbours, especially Igbogbo, against the 1864 to 1865 Egba attack on Ikorodu.
cards.question: Which neighbouring area would you call first if you needed backup?
cards.source_title: Trade, Violence and Diplomacy on the Coast of Ikorodu (Yoruba Studies Review)

cards.name: Zumratul Grammar School
cards.known_for: Keeps Igbogbo's study culture strong
cards.lore: Books, discipline and a 90-year-old society behind you. Serious business.
cards.fact: Igbogbo has a grammar school set up by the Zumratul Islamiyyah Society, an Islamic society that marked its 90th anniversary in 2018.
cards.question: Which school in your area has the most famous old students?

cards.name: The Monarch's History Book
cards.known_for: Keeps Igbogbo's story safe between two covers
cards.lore: Kabiyesi no just make history, him write am down too.
cards.fact: At his 10th coronation anniversary in July 2026, the Adeboruwa launched his book, The Town, the Throne, and Transformations, which documents the history of Igbogbo Kingdom.
cards.question: If your area got its own history book, which chapter would you write?
cards.source_title: Dignitaries celebrate Adeboruwa's 10 years on throne (The Guardian Nigeria)

cards.name: Egbin Power Station
cards.known_for: Keeps fans spinning across the national grid
cards.lore: Six units, one big job: keep the fan spinning.
cards.fact: Egbin Power Station at Egbin/Ijede has six 220 MW units, giving it 1,320 MW of installed capacity. Its first unit came online in 1985.
cards.question: What is the first thing you switch on when the light comes back?
cards.geo_note: moved about 300 m to a viewpoint outside the power zone

cards.name: Egbin Goes Private
cards.known_for: Turns a public plant into a private powerhouse
cards.lore: Same Egbin, new landlords. The turbines no even notice.
cards.fact: In November 2013, Egbin was handed to a joint venture of Sahara Power Group and South Korea's KEPCO under the privatisation of Nigeria's power sector.
cards.question: If you owned a power plant, what would you name it?

cards.name: Ijede General Hospital
cards.known_for: Upgrades itself from clinic to hospital
cards.lore: Started small in 1983, now na full general hospital. Ijede grow am well.
cards.fact: Ijede General Hospital, on Egbin Thermal Power Station Road, began as a primary health centre in 1983 and officially became a general hospital in 2012.
cards.question: What service would you add first to your local hospital?
cards.source_title: Quality Healthcare is Local: The Ijede General Hospital Story (Nigeria Health Watch)

cards.name: Ijede Spring
cards.known_for: Makes a quiet stream feel like a holiday
cards.lore: Ijede get its own spring. Nobody tell Ikogosi.
cards.fact: Ijede Spring, also called Odoro spring, is listed by Lagos State as a gazetted tourism site. Its stream runs beside a beach before emptying into the Lagos Lagoon.
cards.question: What hidden natural spot in Lagos should more people know about?
cards.geo_note: place not found, centre of its area

cards.name: Baba Odoro
cards.known_for: Finds water when everybody else don give up
cards.lore: Drought come, Baba Odoro find water. Legend behaviour.
cards.fact: Local tradition credits an elder, Baba Odoro, with discovering Ijede's spring during a severe drought, which is why it is also known as Odoro spring.
cards.question: Who is the legendary elder people still talk about in your area?
cards.source_title: List of cultural assets in Lagos (Wikipedia)

cards.name: Eyibi Festival
cards.known_for: Renews community bonds every single year
cards.lore: Respect the rites, respect the elders, and check the dates before you plan.
cards.fact: Oke Eletu in Ijede LCDA holds the yearly Eyibi Festival, focused on unity, peace and spiritual renewal. The 2024 edition opened on 15 October with the Ituworo ceremony.
cards.question: How does your community mark a fresh start each year?

cards.name: Egbin Royal Palace
cards.known_for: Hosts royalty and megawatts on the same street
cards.lore: Royal palace on one side, power station on the other. Egbin get range.
cards.fact: The Obateru of Egbin's Royal Palace, centre of traditional authority for the Egbin Kingdom in Ijede LCDA, stands opposite the Lagos Lagoon next to the Egbin power station.
cards.question: What would you put in a museum about your area's history?
cards.geo_note: place not found, centre of its area

cards.name: Ijede Since 1937
cards.known_for: Survives every map redraw since 1937
cards.lore: Ijede don dey run council business since 1937. Senior council, abeg.
cards.fact: Ijede's local government story starts with the Ijede Native Authority of 1937. An Ijede Local Council was gazetted in 1952, and Ijede became an LCDA in 2003.
cards.question: What is the oldest thing in your area that still works?

cards.name: Ijede's Farm Villages
cards.known_for: Feeds the neighbourhood straight from the farm
cards.lore: One LCDA, plenty villages, everybody get farm story.
cards.fact: Ijede LCDA takes in communities such as Ijede, Egbin, Oke Eletu, Ginti, Igbodu, Abule Eko, Igbopa and Ayetoro, whose people are traditionally farmers.
cards.question: Which of these community names would you love to know the story behind?

cards.name: The Ranodu of Imota
cards.known_for: Starts a whole kingdom from one bold move
cards.lore: Imota said make we build our own, and they actually did it.
cards.fact: Imota's Oba carries the title Ranodu. Tradition says the first Ranodu, a son of the Awujale Obaruwa, led his people out of Ijebu-Ode to found a separate kingdom.
cards.question: If you founded your own town, what title would your ruler carry?

cards.name: Near the Ota Tree
cards.known_for: Puts a whole town on the map with one tree
cards.lore: Some towns take their name from kings. Imota took its own from a tree.
cards.fact: Imota's name is traced to 'Imu-Ota', meaning 'near the Ota tree', after the spot where Ranodu's migrating party settled.
cards.question: What landmark would your street be named after?

cards.name: The Ota Wood Rule
cards.known_for: Protects a tree with the power of tradition
cards.lore: That tree na family, so e no dey enter the firewood pile.
cards.fact: Imota tradition holds that residents must not make fire with wood from the Ota tree, the tree linked to the town's name.
cards.question: What family tradition do you keep even if nobody explained why?

cards.name: Agbala Imota
cards.known_for: Leaves its name behind wherever it rests
cards.lore: Imota left a forwarding address near Sagamu and people still use am.
cards.fact: Leaving Ijebu-Ode, Ranodu's party paused at Idado near Sagamu, where he paid homage to the Akarigbo. Tradition says Idado is still known today as Agbala Imota.
cards.question: Which place carries a trace of your family's journey?

cards.name: Imota's Four Quarters
cards.known_for: Splits into four and still stays one
cards.lore: Four quarters, one town. Pick your side for the street football.
cards.fact: Imota town is divided into four quarters: Itun-Opopo, Itun-Onabu, Itun-Maja and Atere.
cards.question: If your area had quarters, what would you name yours?

cards.name: Eko Rice
cards.known_for: Puts a Lagos label on your Sunday rice
cards.lore: Eko Rice don land from Imota straight to your pot.
cards.fact: Rice from the Imota rice mill is sold under the Eko Rice trademark, Lagos State's own rice brand.
cards.question: Local rice or foreign rice: which one wins in your house?
cards.geo_note: place not found, centre of its area
cards.source_title: Lagos to commence sale of Eko Rice this week (BusinessDay)

cards.name: Caleb University
cards.known_for: Turns Imota into a student town every semester
cards.lore: From take-off site to 110 hectares in Imota. Big campus energy.
cards.fact: Caleb University got its provisional licence in May 2007, began classes in January 2008 and moved to its 110-hectare permanent campus at Imota in November 2009.
cards.question: What course would you study if you went back to school tomorrow?

cards.name: Oga the Hunter
cards.known_for: Turns one hunting trip into a whole kingdom
cards.lore: One elephant, one hunter, one whole town. Talk about a first impression.
cards.fact: Local history says Ikorodu was founded by Oga, a hunter from Offin in Sagamu, who killed a dangerous elephant on the Oko Odu farmland and later returned with his brothers Lasunwon and Rademo to settle.
cards.question: If you founded a town today, what would people name it after?

cards.name: Oko Odu: The Odu Farm
cards.known_for: Dyes any cloth deep and dark
cards.lore: Started as a dye farm, became a big city. Ikorodu always knew how to add colour.
cards.fact: The name Ikorodu is traced to Oko Odu, Yoruba for 'Odu farm'. Odu was a plant used to dye cloth, and the Remo accent turned Oko Odu into Okorodu, which later became Ikorodu.
cards.question: Which Lagos place name do you think has the best origin story?

cards.name: The Ayangburen's Palace
cards.known_for: Hosts royal banquets without breaking a sweat
cards.lore: Built by the people, for the crown. Na teamwork make the dream work.
cards.fact: The Ayangburen is the paramount traditional ruler of Ikorodu. A new palace for the throne was commissioned in August 2018, built by Ikorodu indigenes and well-wishers of the community.
cards.question: What would you ask a king if you had five minutes in his palace?

cards.name: Lasunwon and Rademo
cards.known_for: Keeps the royal family tree in perfect order
cards.lore: Two royal houses, three quarters, one town. The maths is mathing.
cards.fact: Ikorodu's traditional town is grouped into three main quarters, Ijomu, Aga and Isele, and the right to the Ikorodu throne belongs to two royal families, Lasunwon and Rademo.
cards.question: Do you know which quarter or family compound your people come from?
cards.source_title: Trade, Violence and Diplomacy on the Coast of Ikorodu (Yoruba Studies Review, 2021)

cards.name: Battle of Ikorodu, 1865
cards.known_for: Builds alliances faster than enemies can march
cards.lore: Ikorodu told a whole army 'not today'. Respect the coast.
cards.fact: In 1865 an Egba army attacking Ikorodu was defeated. Britannica credits troops from Lagos, while a 2021 study credits war chief Balogun Mabadeje Jaiyesimi and his alliance with nearby Igbogbo.
cards.question: When a town wins a battle, who deserves the credit: the generals or the people?
cards.source_title: Trade, Violence and Diplomacy on the Coast of Ikorodu (Yoruba Studies Review)

cards.name: Ceded to the Crown, 1894
cards.known_for: Redraws a state boundary with one signature
cards.lore: One treaty later, Ikorodu was officially on the Lagos side of the map.
cards.fact: After Britain defeated Ijebu in 1892, its lagoon territory passed to the British Crown by two treaties: Epe in 1892, then Ikorodu and its surroundings in 1894. This set the eastern edge of today's Lagos State.
cards.question: How different would Lagos be if Ikorodu had never joined it?
cards.source_title: British Annexation of Epe and Ikorodu, 1892-94 (University of Lagos repository)

cards.name: The I in IBILE
cards.known_for: Holds down a letter in the most famous Lagos acronym
cards.lore: Without Ikorodu, IBILE na just BILE. Nobody wants that.
cards.fact: IBILE stands for Lagos State's five administrative divisions: Ikeja, Badagry, Ikorodu, Lagos and Epe. An edict of April 1968 created them, making Ikorodu one of the five.
cards.question: Can you name all five IBILE divisions without checking your phone?
cards.source_title: Lagos Speaker, Lawmakers at Loggerheads over Administrative Divisions Bill (ThisDay)

cards.name: Ikorodu Oga Festival
cards.known_for: Turns a whole town into one big carnival
cards.lore: A whole week of carnival in Ikorodu. Clear your calendar and charge your phone.
cards.fact: Launched in 1992, the Ikorodu Oga Festival celebrates the town's heritage, usually over a week of processions with traditional dancers, musicians and masquerades.
cards.question: Which hometown festival would you travel back for, no matter what?

cards.name: Oro Day
cards.known_for: Brings a busy town to a respectful pause
cards.lore: On Oro day, Ikorodu keeps its traditions close. Plan your errands early.
cards.fact: Oro is a sacred Yoruba tradition kept by male indigenes. In Ikorodu, Oro day falls during the Magbo festival, and custom asks women to stay indoors while the rites take place.
cards.question: How can old traditions and modern city life make room for each other?
cards.source_title: Female ban during Nigerian festival causes uproar (News24 / AFP)

cards.name: Odun-Osu Festival
cards.known_for: Opens the festival season like a royal starting gun
cards.lore: Odun-Osu opens the festival season. Everybody else, please wait your turn.
cards.fact: Odun-Osu is the first traditional festival of Ikorodu's year and opens the season of other celebrations. It is a royal festival led by the Ayangburen.
cards.question: What is the first big celebration of the year in your family?

cards.name: Farm to Lagos
cards.known_for: Fills Lagos pots before breakfast
cards.lore: Before the food reaches your Lagos pot, Ikorodu don already gather am.
cards.fact: Britannica describes Ikorodu as a collecting point for locally produced fish, poultry, cassava, corn, vegetables and palm oil, which are shipped on to Lagos.
cards.question: What is the best thing you have ever bought straight from a farm?

cards.name: LASUSTECH
cards.known_for: Upgrades itself every few decades without stress
cards.lore: College to poly to university. That is a glow up with certificates.
cards.fact: Lagos State University of Science and Technology began in 1977 as the Lagos State College of Science and Technology, became LASPOTECH in 1986 and turned university under a law signed in 2022.
cards.question: Poly or university: which one has the better campus stories?
cards.source_title: History (Lagos State University of Science and Technology)

cards.name: Ikorodu City FC
cards.known_for: Scores the big goal exactly when it matters
cards.lore: From the lower league to the top flight. Ikorodu don land for NPFL.
cards.fact: Ikorodu City FC won promotion to the Nigeria Premier Football League in June 2024, sealing it with a 2-0 win over Madiba FC in the NNL Super 8 playoffs in Enugu.
cards.question: Would you rather support your local club or a big European side?
cards.geo_note: place not found, centre of its area
cards.source_title: Ikorodu City, Beyond Limits FC gain promotion to NPFL (TheCable)

cards.name: Ikorodu North LCDA
cards.known_for: Holds down the northern end of the Ikorodu story
cards.lore: Ikorodu got so big it needed six councils. North said, 'I go take this side.'
cards.fact: Ikorodu North is one of six councils formed when the old Ikorodu Local Government was split in 2003, alongside Ikorodu, Ikorodu West, Ijede, Imota and Igbogbo-Bayeku.
cards.question: Do you know which council area your street falls under?
cards.geo_note: Ikorodu North not found, Odogunyan stands in

cards.name: Isiu and the Eweye
cards.known_for: Keeps its own crown inside a crowded kingdom
cards.lore: Different town, different crown. Isiu answers to the Eweye.
cards.fact: Isiu is a town in Ikorodu North LCDA, and its traditional ruler carries the title Eweye of Isiu.
cards.question: How many traditional titles from around Lagos can you name?
cards.source_title: NSCDC Lagos Command groundbreaking in Imota, Isiu (The Mirror)

cards.name: Odogunyan
cards.known_for: Runs on factory shifts and big dreams
cards.lore: Odogunyan means business. Ask the factories.
cards.fact: Ikorodu-born economist Temitope Oshikoya described the Odogunyan area of Ikorodu as one of the largest industrial estates in Nigeria.
cards.question: What product would you love to see made in Ikorodu?

cards.name: Ebuwawa Market
cards.known_for: Keeps the market fresh, from tomatoes to taps
cards.lore: Clean water for the market. Wash your hands, then price your tomatoes.
cards.fact: Traders at Ebuwawa Market in Ikorodu North LCDA received solar-powered water and sanitation facilities under a WaterAid Nigeria project funded by the PepsiCo Foundation.
cards.question: What is one thing every Lagos market should have?
cards.geo_note: place and Ebuwawa not found, Odogunyan stands in
cards.source_title: WaterAid hands over solar-powered WASH facilities in Ikorodu North LCDA (Radio Nigeria Lagos)

cards.name: Omigo Solar Borehole
cards.known_for: Turns sunshine into tap water
cards.lore: Sun comes up, water comes out. Omigo is running on solar.
cards.fact: Omigo, a community in Ikorodu North LCDA, received a 20,000-litre solar-powered borehole from WaterAid Nigeria, expected to supply clean water to about 1,200 residents.
cards.question: If your street got one new facility tomorrow, what should it be?
cards.geo_note: Omigo not found, Odogunyan stands in
cards.source_title: Omigo Community Gets 20,000-Litre Solar-Powered Water Facility (Radio Nigeria Lagos)

cards.name: Ikorodu West LCDA
cards.known_for: Ties many communities together with one council stamp
cards.lore: Seven communities, one council, plenty of 'which bus stop you dey?'
cards.fact: Ikorodu West LCDA is made up of communities including Owutu, Asolo, Isawo, Ojokoro, Agbede, Ori-Okuta and Igbo-Olomu.
cards.question: Which of these Ikorodu West communities have you been to?
cards.geo_note: Ikorodu West not found, Owutu stands in
cards.source_title: Ikorodu residents bemoan flood in community (ICIR)

cards.name: Owutu
cards.known_for: Always one short walk from the bus stop
cards.lore: Drop at Agric, waka small, you don reach Owutu.
cards.fact: Owutu sits beside Ikorodu's Agric bus stop and is home to a number of the communities that make up Ikorodu West.
cards.question: Which Lagos bus stop name confuses visitors the most?
cards.source_title: Ikorodu residents bemoan flood in community (ICIR)

cards.name: Isawo and the Oke-Afa
cards.known_for: Crosses rivers like they are just another bus stop
cards.lore: When the Oke-Afa rises, Isawo people know: plan your route early.
cards.fact: Isawo, in Ikorodu West, lies on the Agric-Isawo Road, where the Oke-Afa River overflows in the rainy season. Residents have long pushed for the Afa bridge and the road to be completed.
cards.question: What is the most important bridge on your daily journey?
cards.source_title: Ikorodu residents beg Sanwo-Olu to fix bad roads (Peoples Gazette)

cards.name: Konu
cards.known_for: Plots shortcuts across state lines
cards.lore: Konu already drew the shortcut. Lagos-Ibadan traffic, take note.
cards.fact: Konu residents in Ikorodu West have called for a bridge linking Konu to Ibafo in Ogun State, as a relief route away from the congested Lagos-Ibadan Expressway.
cards.question: If you could build one shortcut anywhere in Lagos, where would it go?
cards.geo_note: Konu not found, Owutu stands in
cards.source_title: Residents seek bridge to link Ishawo, Ibafo (The Guardian Nigeria)

cards.name: Igbolomu New Yam
cards.known_for: Brings South East harvest vibes to the Ikorodu side
cards.lore: Yam don land for Igbolomu. Thanksgiving with Ogene is non-negotiable.
cards.fact: Igbo residents of Igbolomu, Ikorodu, celebrate the New Yam Festival through the Igboamaka Progressives Association, with families giving thanks for the harvest and an Ogene dance.
cards.question: Which festival from another part of Nigeria have you celebrated in Lagos?
cards.geo_note: Igbolomu not found, Owutu stands in
cards.source_title: Igboamaka Progressives Association celebrates New Yam Festival in Lagos (Primetime Reporters)

cards.name: Pen Cinema
cards.known_for: Names a bridge long after the last film rolled
cards.lore: Before Netflix, na Pen Cinema be Agege big screen.
cards.fact: Pen Cinema in Agege was one of the few Lagos cinema houses still running in the early 1990s. Its name lives on in the 1.4 km Pen Cinema Bridge, a flyover project started in 2017.
cards.question: What was the first film you ever watched in a cinema?
cards.geo_note: place not found, centre of its area
cards.source_title: Is This the Age of Nollywood at Domestic Box Office? (Afrocritik)

cards.name: Agege Proper
cards.known_for: Was Agege before Agege was Agege
cards.lore: Before Agege get station, Orile don dey here.
cards.fact: Orile-Agege is the original homestead of the Agege community, settled by Awori people. Orile means 'proper', setting it apart from the newer town that grew around the railway station built between 1895 and 1911.
cards.question: Which part of your area is the oldest, and how do you know?

cards.name: Orile Festivals
cards.known_for: Keeps the old drums talking
cards.lore: Na Orile old drums still dey talk.
cards.fact: Orile-Agege is tied to older Yoruba religious traditions, with ancient deities and festivals that include Egungun and Gelede, local history says.
cards.question: Which festival do you remember most from growing up?

cards.name: Biggest Council
cards.known_for: Never runs out of new streets
cards.lore: If you don enter Alimosho, you don enter plenty Lagos.
cards.fact: Alimosho, set up in 1945 under the old Western Region, is widely described as the largest local government in Lagos. The 2006 census counted 1,288,714 people, but Lagos State said the true figure was over 2 million.
cards.question: How many Lagos LGAs can you name without checking?

cards.name: Born 1996
cards.known_for: Guards the Lagos side of the Ogun border
cards.lore: One leg for Lagos, the other near Ogun. Na Ifako style.
cards.fact: Ifako-Ijaiye Local Government was created on 1 October 1996, carved out of Agege, with its headquarters at Ifako. It is a border area that shares a boundary with Ogun State.
cards.question: Which border town have you crossed from Lagos into Ogun?

cards.name: Iju Waterworks
cards.known_for: Has filled Lagos buckets for over a century
cards.lore: Before sachet water, na Iju dey pour Lagos tap.
cards.fact: Iju Waterworks was Lagos's first piped water scheme, built mainly to serve colonial residents of Ikoyi. Its first plant, from 1910, drew spring water from the Iju hills at about 2.4 million gallons a day.
cards.question: Where does the water in your house come from?
cards.geo_note: Iju Water Works is just across the border in Ogun State, so Iju stands in
cards.source_title: A Background of Water Management in Lagos (Lafayette College Hydronarratives)

cards.name: Agege's Western Edge
cards.known_for: Stands guard where Lagos meets Egbaland
cards.lore: Na Agbado be the old border post. Abeokuta dey the other side.
cards.fact: Agbado once marked the western edge of the old Agege territory, where it met Abeokuta district, according to a description tied to an 1842 map of the Lagos district.
cards.question: Where do you think your area's old border used to be?

cards.name: Old Ayobo
cards.known_for: Remembers Lagos before the expressway
cards.lore: Ayobo no be new area, e get deep roots.
cards.fact: Ayobo is counted among the old Awori settlements of ancient Agege, alongside Orile, Ogba and Ikola. Local history says these communities came under the authority of the Baale Alaige.
cards.question: What is the oldest family story you know about your area?

cards.name: First Council Office
cards.known_for: Holds the first key to Alimosho
cards.lore: Before Alimosho split into six, na here e start.
cards.fact: The first office block of the old single Alimosho Local Government, a two-storey building on Council Street, now lies within Egbe-Idimu LCDA.
cards.question: Where is the oldest public building in your area?
cards.geo_note: place not found, centre of its area

cards.name: Kudaki and Akeja
cards.known_for: Runs on two family trees and one town spirit
cards.lore: Two warriors from Ife plant Egbe. Their families still dey hold am.
cards.fact: Local history says Egbe, once called Igbe, was founded in the 17th century by two warriors from Ile-Ife, Kudaki and Akeja. Their descendants make up the town's two ruling houses.
cards.question: Which family names in your area go back the furthest?
cards.source_title: I Had My First Degree at 58 Years (ThisDay via PressReader)

cards.name: Three Anthills
cards.known_for: Named by the hardest workers in the bush
cards.lore: Na anthill give Igando im name. No be small thing.
cards.fact: Local history says Igando was founded about 600 years ago by Bini migrants from Eru-Etan village. The settlers found three anthills, called 'Igan-Odo' in Yoruba, and the name Igando grew from them.
cards.question: Do you know the story behind your area's name?

cards.name: Mosan Roots
cards.known_for: Links the new mainland to old Awori roots
cards.lore: Mosan get history pass im new estates.
cards.fact: Local history says Mosan was one of the communities that later joined the old Awori settlements of ancient Agege, which came under the authority of the Baale Alaige.
cards.question: Which old family names do you still hear in your area?
cards.geo_note: Mosan not found, Alimosho stands in

cards.name: Village of the Egba
cards.known_for: Carries Abeokuta in its name
cards.lore: Egba people land first, Abule Egba carry the name.
cards.fact: Abule Egba was first called 'Abule awon Egba', Yoruba for 'village of the Egba people', after early settlers who came from Abeokuta, local history says.
cards.question: Does your area's name tell you who settled there first?
cards.source_title: History behind the names of 10 popular places in Lagos (Ripples Nigeria)

cards.name: Oko-Oba Abattoir
cards.known_for: Keeps Lagos pots full of meat
cards.lore: Your Sunday stew meat fit don pass Oko-Oba first.
cards.fact: The Lagos State Central Abattoir at Oko-Oba is the largest of the state's eight authorised abattoirs. BusinessDay reports that over 30 percent of the roughly 8,000 cattle and ruminants eaten in Lagos daily are slaughtered there.
cards.question: Suya, asun or pepper soup: which Lagos meat dish wins?

cards.name: Aro Meta
cards.known_for: Gives every newcomer the Lagos once over
cards.lore: The three elders dey watch every Johnny Just Come wey enter.
cards.fact: Aro Meta, the statue of three Lagos white-cap chiefs over 12 ft tall, was made by sculptor Bodun Shodeinde in 1991 and first stood opposite Ojodu-Berger bus stop to welcome people entering Lagos.
cards.question: What advice would you give someone arriving in Lagos for the first time?
cards.geo_note: place not found, centre of its area

cards.name: Kalakuta Museum
cards.known_for: Plays Afrobeat even when the speakers are off
cards.lore: Na here Abami Eda rest im head. The music never sleep.
cards.fact: Fela's three-storey home at 7 Gbemisola Street, off Allen Avenue, opened as the Kalakuta Republic Museum on 15 October 2012, his 74th birthday. It shows his clothes, instruments and artwork.
cards.question: Which Fela song would you play to welcome a visitor to Lagos?

cards.name: LUTH Idi-Araba
cards.known_for: Trains doctors and heals the mainland at the same time
cards.lore: Idi-Araba wards don see Lagos through every kind of night.
cards.fact: Lagos University Teaching Hospital opened in 1962 at Idi-Araba, on a 92-acre site once occupied by the Mainland Hospital. It grew from a 1961 federal plan to build a full medical school in Lagos.
cards.question: Who is the doctor or nurse your family always calls first?

cards.name: Mushin Name
cards.known_for: Hides a whole fruit inside one name
cards.lore: Before all the hustle, na fruit picking give Mushin im name.
cards.fact: Local history says the name Mushin comes from 'mu ishin', Yoruba for picking the ishin fruit. The area later grew into one of the busiest suburbs on the Lagos mainland.
cards.question: Which Lagos place name do you think has the best story?

cards.name: Oshodi Tapa
cards.known_for: Turns a war captain into the bus stop everyone shouts
cards.lore: Every conductor wey shout 'Oshodi!' dey call a war captain name.
cards.fact: Local history says Oshodi takes its name from Chief Oshodi Tapa, a Nupe-born child raised in the Lagos palace who became war captain to Oba Kosoko and led the 1845 siege known as the Salt Water War.
cards.question: Which Lagos bus stop name has the wildest backstory you know?

cards.name: Shomolu Printing District
cards.known_for: Prints your wedding programme overnight
cards.lore: You need 500 flyers by morning? Shomolu no dey sleep.
cards.fact: Shomolu is Lagos's printing capital, with offset and digital print shops packed along Bajulaiye Road and Oguntolu. A 2016 count found about 200 print shops, many in small kiosks attached to homes.
cards.question: What's the last thing you got printed in a rush?

cards.name: Agboyi Creek Escape
cards.known_for: Hides a fleeing king in plain water
cards.lore: Even war captain fit show mercy for Agboyi water.
cards.fact: In 1845, after Kosoko's forces besieged his palace in the Salt Water War, Oba Akitoye fled north across the lagoon. Kosoko's war captain Oshodi Tapa granted him safe passage through the Agboyi Creek.
cards.question: Who showed you mercy when they didn't have to?

cards.name: Agboyi Villages
cards.known_for: Keeps six villages under one crown
cards.lore: Six villages, one Oba, and the river dey watch everything.
cards.fact: Local history says Agboyi was founded by Odoyi, who left the old Awori town of Isheri. Today it is a riverside community of six villages, with its Oba seated at Agboyi 1.
cards.question: Which Lagos waterside community have you visited?
cards.source_title: Pains of Neglect in Agboyi Community (ThisDay)

cards.name: Kosi Kosi
cards.known_for: Never hides a thing from a guest
cards.lore: For Ikosi, nothing dey hide from visitor. Kosi kosi!
cards.fact: Local history says Ikosi was founded in the 17th century by Aina Ejo, son of Ile-Ife prince Akanbiogun. Folklore says the name is short for 'Kosi Kosi', the settlers' promise to visitors that nothing was hoarded.
cards.question: What does the name of your area mean?

cards.name: Ojuwoye Market
cards.known_for: Stretches small money into a full bag
cards.lore: Ojuwoye price go make you buy wetin you no plan.
cards.fact: Ojuwoye Market in Mushin Olosha is known for its wide range of affordable goods. It is counted among notable Lagos markets alongside Oshodi and Tejuosho.
cards.question: What's the cheapest good thing you ever bought at a market?
cards.geo_note: place not found, centre of its area

cards.name: Ojuwoye Town
cards.known_for: Keeps Mushin's centre beating
cards.lore: Mushin get many corners, but Ojuwoye na the heartbeat.
cards.fact: Ojuwoye Town is described as the centre of Mushin, the crowded mainland suburb about 10 km north of Lagos city centre beside the main road to Ikeja.
cards.question: Where is the true centre of your neighbourhood?

cards.name: Jakande Estate Oke-Afa
cards.known_for: Turns renters into homeowners
cards.lore: Baba Kekere build am, Oke-Afa people still dey call am home.
cards.fact: Jakande Estate at Oke-Afa is one of the low-cost housing estates built under Lateef Jakande, Lagos's first civilian governor. A 2023 tribute dates its opening to December 1983, days before the military took power.
cards.question: Did anyone in your family live in a Jakande estate?
cards.geo_note: place not found, centre of its area

cards.name: Ifoshi Road
cards.known_for: Carries all of Ejigbo to the expressway
cards.lore: For Ejigbo, once you reach Ifoshi, you don almost reach house.
cards.fact: Ifoshi Road is Ejigbo's main access route, linking the community to the Oshodi-Apapa Expressway through the Ikotun-Ejigbo junction. After more than two decades in poor shape, it was rebuilt and reopened in September 2024.
cards.question: Which road takes you home, and what do you see on it?
cards.source_title: Ifoshi Road Gets Facelift After 26 Years (ThisDay)

cards.name: Isolo General Hospital
cards.known_for: Patches up Isolo, from first cry to check-up
cards.lore: When Isolo body no correct, na here people dey run go.
cards.fact: Isolo General Hospital is a Lagos State public hospital serving Isolo and nearby areas with emergency, maternity and outpatient care, plus specialist treatment.
cards.question: What's one thing that would make Lagos hospitals better?

cards.name: FCE (Technical) Akoka
cards.known_for: Turns technicians into teachers
cards.lore: Na here Lagos technical teachers dey learn how to teach.
cards.fact: Founded by the federal government in 1967, this Akoka college trains teachers for technical, vocational and commercial subjects. It started life as the National Technical Teachers College.
cards.question: Which teacher made a subject finally click for you?

cards.name: Crown Troupe of Africa
cards.known_for: Turns any open street into a theatre
cards.lore: For Bariga, the street na stage and everybody na audience.
cards.fact: Bariga is home base of Crown Troupe of Africa, a total theatre company blending dance, drama, music and Yoruba masquerade style. Its Bariga Open Air Theatre carnival grew into the Eko Theatre Festival.
cards.question: Have you ever watched a play performed on the street?
cards.geo_note: place not found, centre of its area
cards.source_title: 2018 Eko Theatre Festival rounds off today (The Guardian Nigeria)

cards.name: Apapa Amusement Park
cards.known_for: Turns any Sunday into Christmas
cards.lore: Na here plenty Lagos pikin first scream for ride.
cards.fact: Apapa Amusement Park opened in 1976 as Lagos Lunar Park, jointly owned by the Lagos Island and Lagos Mainland councils with a Swiss firm, Improjex. It reopened after a full makeover in 2015.
cards.question: Which fun-fair ride would you queue the longest for?

cards.name: Apapa: Fishing Village to Port Town
cards.known_for: Grew from canoe to container ship
cards.lore: Before container, na canoe and fish rule Apapa.
cards.fact: Apapa began as a small fishing village of the Awori, a Yoruba subgroup. Under British rule it grew into a port town, with a low-density Government Reserved Area built for colonial administrators and technical staff.
cards.question: What do you think Apapa looked like before the port came?

cards.name: Epetedo
cards.known_for: Remembers every compound by name
cards.lore: Na here Kosoko people settle when dem come back home.
cards.fact: Epetedo was founded on 16 September 1862 by followers of Oba Kosoko, led by Chief Oshodi Tapa, after about a decade away. Local history says the name points to early settlers from Epe.
cards.question: Which Lagos Island street do you think has the best stories?
cards.geo_note: Epetedo not found, Lagos Island stands in
cards.source_title: Lagos Islanders, Epetedo residents celebrate 155 years of existence (The Guardian Nigeria)

cards.name: The Epetedo Declaration
cards.known_for: Speaks louder than any annulment
cards.lore: Na here June 12 talk loud pass.
cards.fact: On 11 June 1994, MKO Abiola declared himself president-elect at the Eleganza Sport Centre in Epetedo, a year after the 12 June 1993 election was annulled. The speech led to his arrest.
cards.question: What does June 12 mean to you?
cards.geo_note: place and Epetedo not found, Lagos Island stands in
cards.source_title: Epetedo community relives Abiola's historic declaration 24 years after (The Guardian Nigeria)

cards.name: Surulere: Patience Pays
cards.known_for: Rewards anyone who waits small
cards.lore: Na patience build Surulere, na patience go reward you.
cards.fact: Surulere roughly means patience and perseverance in Yoruba. Its New Lagos area, also called the Surulere Re-Housing Estate, was among the first public housing projects in Nigeria.
cards.question: What is the best thing you ever got because you waited?

cards.name: Ikoyi Club 1938
cards.known_for: Mixes the first glass of Chapman
cards.lore: Na here Chapman first enter glass, local history talk am.
cards.fact: Ikoyi Club 1938 dates its founding to 29 September 1938, when the European Club and the Lagos Golf Club came together. Wikipedia credits the Chapman cocktail to Sam Alamutu, who first mixed it on the club grounds.
cards.question: Chapman or Zobo: which one wins at a Lagos party?

cards.name: Dodan Barracks
cards.known_for: Kept the keys to the country for decades
cards.lore: Na here Naija power sleep for over twenty years.
cards.fact: Dodan Barracks in Ikoyi, named after a Second World War battle site in Burma, was Nigeria's seat of government under military rule from 1966. The seat of government moved from there to Abuja on 12 December 1991.
cards.question: Which Lagos building do you think has seen the most history?
cards.geo_note: moved about 120 m to a viewpoint outside the military zone

cards.name: Coker: Named for a Family
cards.known_for: Keeps the factories humming
cards.lore: Na one family name, now na whole bus stop.
cards.fact: Wikipedia says Lagos's Coker district is named after the Coker family, long led by Justice G. B. A. Coker. Coker, with Iponri and Iganmu, is also where most of Surulere's industrial firms sit.
cards.question: Which Lagos street or area is named after a family you know?

cards.name: Aguda: The Returnees' Name
cards.known_for: Carries a Brazil story in its name
cards.lore: Who dey Aguda today fit get Bahia story for blood.
cards.fact: Aguda is the Yoruba name for freed Africans who came back from Brazil, in use in Lagos from about 1835. Surulere's history records Aguda and Saro returnees from Brazil and Cuba settling in Surulere in the 19th century.
cards.question: Do you know any Lagos family with Brazilian roots?
cards.geo_note: Aguda not found, Surulere stands in

cards.name: Itire and the Onitire
cards.known_for: Wears its own crown on the Mainland
cards.lore: Itire get Kabiyesi, no be small place o.
cards.fact: Itire is one of Surulere's quarters with its own recognised traditional ruler, the Onitire of Itire. A 2023 essay on Lagos institutions lists the Onitire alongside the Oniru of Iruland and the Elegushi of Ikateland.
cards.question: Do you know who the traditional ruler of your area is?

cards.name: Maracana Stadium
cards.known_for: Turns street ballers into Super Eagles
cards.lore: Na for this ground Ajegunle legends learn to dribble the world.
cards.fact: Odion Ighalo, Samson Siasia, Obafemi Martins and Taribo West all played at Ajegunle's Maracana ground. By 2023 an upgrade had turned the old dumpsite into a centre with 19 pitches and hostels with 192 beds.
cards.question: Which Ajegunle footballer would make your all-time Super Eagles team?
cards.geo_note: place not found, centre of its area
cards.source_title: Ambode to Give Ajegunle's Maracana Stadium Status (ThisDay)

cards.name: AJ Music
cards.known_for: Gets the whole street dancing galala
cards.lore: Who never dance galala never reach AJ City.
cards.fact: AJ music, a blend of Esan samba, reggae and jazz, is Ajegunle's own sound. Producer John 'Mighty Mouse' Oboh (1967 to 2023) pioneered it, and Ajegunle musicians honour him as the Father of AJ Music.
cards.question: Which AJ music or galala tune still gets you on your feet?
cards.source_title: Ajegunle Musicians Honour Mighty Mouse, 'Father of AJ Music' (The Guardian Nigeria)

cards.name: Tolu Schools Complex
cards.known_for: Teaches a small town's worth of students at once
cards.lore: If you school for AJ, Tolu don hear your name before.
cards.fact: Tolu Schools Complex in Ajegunle was set up in 1981 to deliver Lagos State's mass education policy. It now groups 36 public schools in one compound and was recently remodelled.
cards.question: What do you remember most about your secondary school days?
cards.source_title: Lagos begins rehabilitation of dilapidated Tolu school complex, Ajegunle (The Guardian Nigeria)

cards.name: Mosafejo Council Seat
cards.known_for: Keeps Amukoko's paperwork moving
cards.lore: Na Mosafejo be the engine room of Ifelodun.
cards.fact: Created in 2003 out of Ajeromi-Ifelodun, Ifelodun LCDA runs its council from 3 Dispensary Street, Mosafejo, Amukoko. A second coordinating office sits at Layeni on Ojo Road, near Oja bus stop.
cards.question: What is one thing every Lagos neighbourhood needs from its council?
cards.source_title: Addresses of LSETF Liaison Offices by Local Government (Lagos State Employment Trust Fund)

cards.name: Mile 2
cards.known_for: Links the Badagry road to the Island by rail
cards.lore: Mile 2 to Marina by train? Na so Lagos don change.
cards.fact: Mile 2, where the Apapa-Oshodi Expressway meets the Lagos-Badagry Expressway, is the western end of the Blue Line's first phase, which opened to the public on 4 September 2023 with five stations running to Marina.
cards.question: Danfo, BRT or train: how do you cross Mile 2?

cards.name: Trade Fair Complex
cards.known_for: Sells everything from car parts to gold
cards.lore: Anything wey you dey find, Trade Fair get am. Just price am well.
cards.fact: Designed by architect Zoran Bojovic and built by Energoprojekt, the Lagos International Trade Fair Complex in Satellite Town covers over 320 hectares. It was commissioned in 1976, ahead of the first Lagos International Trade Fair in 1977.
cards.question: What is the best thing you ever bought at a Lagos trade fair?

cards.name: Trade Fair Markets
cards.known_for: Finds the spare part nobody else can
cards.lore: If the car part no dey ASPMDA, e never land Nigeria.
cards.fact: In 2002 jewellery, auto spare parts and other traders moved from Balogun Market on Lagos Island into the Trade Fair Complex. It now hosts the Balogun, Progressive and ASPMDA auto spare parts markets.
cards.question: Do you trust your mechanic to buy the part, or do you go to Trade Fair yourself?
cards.source_title: Lagos International Trade Fair Complex (Bureau of Public Enterprises)

cards.name: Oto, Once Ijake
cards.known_for: Remembers the name it had before
cards.lore: Before Oto, na Ijake. Ask any Oto elder.
cards.fact: Local history recorded in a 1939 colonial report says Oto was founded in the 18th century by Benin migrants led by Aregi Ope. First called Ijake, it took the name Oto after a land division at Igbo-Ogo fixed its boundary with Iba.
cards.question: Do you know the old name of the place you grew up?
cards.geo_note: Oto not found, Ijanikin stands in

cards.name: Obadore First Camp
cards.known_for: Where the northern Ojo story starts
cards.lore: Before Ojo spread, na Obadore people first rest their load.
cards.fact: Local history says later Awori migrants from Ile-Ife first settled at Obadore in Iba, then spread west and southwest. Iba and Igbo-Elerin grew as Ojo's northern section, separate from the western Oto-Awori side.
cards.question: Which part of your area do the elders say was settled first?

cards.name: FGC Ijanikin
cards.known_for: Mixes students from every corner of Nigeria
cards.lore: For FGC Ijanikin, Lagos pikin learn to be Nigerian together.
cards.fact: Federal Government College Ijanikin was set up by the Federal Ministry of Education in 1975, giving Lagos a co-educational federal unity school like the other 12 states of the time. Its first principal served from October 1975.
cards.question: Did you go to a boarding school, and what did you miss most from home?

cards.name: Apa
cards.known_for: Older than the town next door
cards.lore: Before Badagry town grow, Apa don dey there.
cards.fact: Founded around the 15th century by Awori migrants, Apa is one of the oldest settlements in Badagry Division and has its own Oba, the Alapa of Apa. Most of its people are of Awori and Ogu heritage.
cards.question: Which languages do you hear spoken in your family besides English?

cards.name: Seme Border
cards.known_for: Opens the road from Lagos to the rest of West Africa
cards.lore: One more step from Seme, and you don cross into Benin.
cards.fact: The Gbaji-Seme axis of Badagry West links Nigeria to Benin Republic at the Seme international border, a major customs revenue point. A 2015 report counted over 50 communities and about 200,000 residents along the corridor.
cards.question: Have you ever travelled to another country by road? Where to?
cards.source_title: 50 Lagos communities lived without electricity for 16 years (Vanguard)

cards.name: St. Matthew's Amukoko
cards.known_for: Opens its classroom to every faith
cards.lore: For Amukoko, St. Matthew's gate open for everybody.
cards.fact: St. Matthew Catholic Church in Amukoko runs a low-fee school for the community and a training unit for girls, youths and teenage mothers, open to people of every faith. Its justice and peace arm has hosted local peace summits.
cards.question: Who in your neighbourhood gives young people a second chance?
cards.geo_note: place not found, centre of its area
cards.source_title: JDPC holds peace summit in Lagos (The Sun)

cards.name: Kayo-Kayo Festival
cards.known_for: Brings the whole of Epe home once a year
cards.lore: Who dey Epe for Kayo-Kayo week? The whole town go dey there.
cards.fact: Kayo-Kayo is a yearly cultural and religious festival in Epe, celebrated by descendants of Oba Kosoko to mark his arrival in Epe in 1851. It is usually held in the first Islamic month, around Ashura.
cards.question: Which festival makes you travel back to your hometown?

cards.name: Epe Barge Builders
cards.known_for: Builds the boats that carry the lagoon trade
cards.lore: Na Epe hand build the boats wey dey run the lagoon.
cards.fact: Epe was set up by the mid-18th century as the chief port for Ijebu-Ode, trading cloth and farm produce. Britannica says the town is best known for building the motorised, shallow-draft barges that move along the coastal lagoons.
cards.question: Have you ever crossed a Lagos lagoon by boat?

cards.name: Akodo Beach
cards.known_for: Gives the Atlantic its own guest house
cards.lore: Akodo sand soft pass your bedsheet, ask anybody wey don go.
cards.fact: Eko Tourist Beach Resort, also called Akodo Beach, was developed at Akodo by the Lagos State government in the 1990s. It sits on about 10 acres with chalets, restaurants and more than half a mile of beach.

cards.name: Alara of Ilara-Epe
cards.known_for: Keeps the crown steady for generations
cards.lore: Na Ilara wait 60 years before e see another crowning.
cards.fact: In 2020 Ilara-Epe installed a new Alara, its first coronation in about 60 years. The previous king, Oba Akeem Okunola Adesanya II, reigned 58 years until October 2018 and was then the longest reigning monarch in Lagos State.

cards.name: Ejinrin Lagoon Market
cards.known_for: Sent the palm oil that Lagos shipped to the world
cards.lore: Before Balogun or Oyingbo, na Ejinrin be the market wey everybody sabi.
cards.fact: Ejinrin was a great market on the north bank of the Lagos Lagoon. Colonial records counted 20,000 to 26,000 people on a market day by the late 1800s, and by 1908 it was rated the largest market in Nigeria's western provinces.

cards.name: Agbowa Refuge Town
cards.known_for: Makes room for everybody who knocks
cards.lore: Na Agbowa open door when war scatter the neighbours.
cards.fact: Local history says Agbowa-Ikosi sheltered people from Imota, Ibefun, Ota and Owu during the old wars, who settled in quarters called Ago-Mota, Ago-Ibefun, Ago-Ota and Ago-Owu. The town was also headquarters of the old Ikosi District Council.

cards.name: Awo Detention Camp
cards.known_for: Turns a place of detention into a place of learning
cards.lore: Local history says Awo pray for this town and the prayer catch.
cards.fact: In 1962 Chief Obafemi Awolowo was restricted to a government rest house in Lekki Town, a site later called the Awolowo Detention Camp. Lagos State remodelled it as an institute in June 2009.

cards.name: Isale Eko Were Roots
cards.known_for: Were and ajiwere, the roots of fuji
cards.lore: Na Ramadan wake up call wey turn to the whole owambe sound.
cards.fact: Fuji grew out of were, also called ajisari, music performed to wake Muslims before dawn in Ramadan. In the early independence years, Isale Eko on Lagos Island had a notable line up of ajiwere performers, before Sikiru Ayinde Barrister turned were into fuji.

cards.name: The Headies
cards.known_for: Nigeria's leading music awards
cards.lore: The night every Naija artist dey pray to carry that head.
cards.fact: The Headies began in 2006 as the Hip Hop World Awards and took its current name in 2011. Its first two editions were held at the Muson Centre in Onikan, Lagos, and the 2010 to 2012 editions at Eko Hotel, Victoria Island.
